Slovak Transportation Equipment Sites Targeted Amid Ongoing Border Blockade

Bratislava, June 12—A prolonged blockade of major transportation equipment manufacturing sites across western Slovakia entered its fourth day Wednesday, with trade officials warning of mounting losses and disruption for the industry’s firms and workers.

The blockade, attributed by Slovak authorities to organized protest groups reportedly aligned with a foreign state, has seen crowds occupy entrances to key plants in Trnava, Nitra, and Žilina. The groups are demanding changes in government policy related to cross-border trade agreements, according to government sources.

Production at major industry firms such as Tatra Engineering, Slovtrans Equip and Novomobil has been suspended since Sunday evening, with management citing “unimpeded access for essential staff and ongoing safety concerns.” Union representatives estimate that more than 7,000 workers have been sent home or are unable to reach their worksites.

“We are deeply concerned for our members,” said Milan Hruška, spokesperson for the Slovak Transportation Equipment Workers’ Union. “Many fear for their jobs if this continues. The plants are silent, and the uncertainty is growing by the hour.”

The Slovak Ministry of Industry stated that negotiations with protest leaders were continuing “but with limited progress.” The government has accused “external actors” of encouraging the unrest, but declined to give further details.

Industry analysts say the blockade is already causing “significant operational losses” across the sector. “If this is not resolved quickly, the impact on Slovakia’s transportation equipment output could be severe,” said Veronika Šimek, senior analyst with Central Europe Industrial Watch.

Plant management at affected sites report no damage to equipment but warn that a protracted halt could lead to maintenance issues and missed international delivery deadlines. There have been no reports of injuries. The situation remains tense, with no immediate resolution in sight.
